about: The models scripts/model-eval.ts tries, besides the rule parser. A starter list: choosing the candidates is a separate research task. Keys go in the repo-root .env under keyEnv (git ignores it). Prices are NOT in this file: there is one dated table of model prices, modules/understanding/rates/<date>.json, which the runtime also reads. A candidate names its provider (the name runtime.json would give it), and the evaluation looks up (provider, model) in that table and prints the cost of 1,000 messages; a model with no line there shows "no price set". Model ids were read from each provider's own docs on 3 Nov 2026 and have not been tried with a key: if every message of a candidate fails with an HTTP error, check the id and extraBody against the provider's docs. The Phase 0 research (docs research/2026-11-phase0-providers-and-accounts.md) recommends testing three first: claude-haiku-5-5, gemini-3.1-flash-lite (paid tier: the free tier's text is used for training, which WhatsApp's terms forbid) and sarvam-105b-conversations. The others are kept in reserve (run them with --only).

candidates.name: claude-haiku-5-5
candidates.note: Anthropic's current fast, low-cost model (the id is from the Claude API model list). Effort low because reading one short message needs no long thinking. Price: from the rate table (provider anthropic).

candidates.name: gemini-3.1-flash-lite
candidates.note: One of the three the Phase 0 research recommends: the best independent evidence on Indian languages among the big labs. Use a paid-tier key; free-tier text is used for training. Reached through Gemini's OpenAI-compatible endpoint (key as a Bearer token). If every message gets HTTP 400, try "responseFormat": "json_object". Price: from the rate table (provider google).

candidates.name: gemini-3.5-flash-lite
candidates.note: The newer Flash-Lite, kept in reserve; reached through Gemini's OpenAI-compatible endpoint (key sent as a Bearer token). Free-tier keys are rate limited: add "pauseMs": 4000 if messages fail with HTTP 429. If every message gets HTTP 400, try "responseFormat": "json_object": whether its compatibility layer accepts a closed strict schema is the least certain part. Price: from the rate table (provider google); thinking tokens count as output.

candidates.name: sarvam-105b-conversations
candidates.note: An Indian-language model, the variant meant for real-time conversation (the other is sarvam-105b). Its docs list both Authorization: Bearer and api-subscription-key and are not consistent: if every message gets HTTP 401 or 403, set "authHeader": "api-subscription-key". Reasoning tokens are billed as output tokens. Price: none in the rate table yet (Sarvam's price page shows display names only), so the cost row says no price set.

candidates.name: groq-gpt-oss-20b
candidates.note: The cheapest production model on Groq's models page with published prices, and one of the models Groq lists for strict JSON-schema output. An open-weight model that may be weaker in Malayalam and Kannada: the eval is how to tell. Price: none in the rate table yet, so the cost row says no price set.

candidates.name: openai-gpt-6-luna
candidates.note: The model OpenAI's models page describes as the most efficient for focused, high-volume tasks. Its request shape was not tried: newer OpenAI models take max_completion_tokens and refuse a set temperature, so extraBody nulls those two. Price: from the rate table (provider openai).

candidates.name: deepinfra-deepseek-v4.1-flash
candidates.note: Step 2 of the understanding (economics note, section 3.2): DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on DeepInfra's Flex tier, the owner's pick. DeepInfra is paid: the key goes only in .env. Price: from the rate table (provider deepinfra: $0.16 in, $0.48 out per million, from the economics note's third-party trackers: check deepinfra.com before choosing). The model id is a best guess at DeepInfra's naming: if every message gets HTTP 404 or 400, copy the id from deepinfra.com, and if 400 try "responseFormat": "json_object".

candidates.name: laya
candidates.note: Step 1: Laya (Apache-2.0 open weights) served on this machine by laya-serve, for example LAYA_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8080 in .env; the steps to run it are in Deferred.md. No key, and nothing leaves the machine. Price: none per call, because it is self-hosted (the rate table says so, dated). Malayalam and Kannada are not on the model card: the table is how to find out.

candidates.name: jev
candidates.note: Step 1, hosted: Jev (TypeSafe). It is paid: the address and the key go only in .env. Price: about $0.042 per million tokens, as the economics note quotes the Laya page, from the rate table (provider jev). The model name clm-latest is the example in pydantic-ai's docs: use the name Jev serves your account's model under.
